stories.headline: Stocks slip from record highs as bond yields jump; Dow drops 341 points
stories.summary: US stocks fell on Wednesday, a day after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at records. Pressure built in the bond market, where Treasury yields touched their highest levels in more than two decades, and investors weighed Federal Reserve minutes pointing to another rate hike. The S&P 500 and the Dow ended five-day winning streaks, and small companies fell hardest.
key_facts: Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 341.41 points, or 0.66%, to 51,179.87
S&P 500 fell 0.22% to 7,801.77, a day after its record close of 7,818.93
Nasdaq Composite fell 0.22% to 27,538.69
Russell 2000 fell 1.31% to about 2,793
The S&P 500 and the Dow snapped five-day winning streaks
S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow 30.6% in the coming reporting season

fact_check.notes: Closing levels for the three main indexes match across CNBC (search excerpt), Benzinga and Investrade. The Russell 2000 figure, the winning-streak detail and the 30.6% earnings estimate come from Investrade only.

stories.headline: Fed minutes: most officials expect another rate hike by year end
stories.summary: Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 meeting, released Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET, showed every official backed the quarter-point rate hike and most thought another increase would likely be appropriate by the end of the year. The minutes gave no signal on timing. Inflation has run above the Fed's target for more than five years.
key_facts: The minutes say: 'Most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end'
The September meeting raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75%-4.00%, by a 12-0 vote
September projections: 12 participants favored one more quarter-point hike in 2026, four favored two more, two favored none
The minutes gave no indication of when the next hike would come
Traders priced roughly 17% odds of a hike at the October 27-28 meeting
Inflation has run above target for more than five years

fact_check.notes: The key sentence and the projection split are reported by The Tribune and IndexBox; the unanimous vote by Bloomberg (headline) and the search excerpt of the Fed's own minutes page. The 17% October odds come from Yahoo Finance's live blog only.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield hits 5.365%, a 24-year high, then eases after a strong auction
stories.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.365% on Wednesday, its highest since April 2002, and the 30-year reached 5.732%, its highest since May 2002. Yields then backed off after the Treasury's $39 billion sale of 10-year notes drew strong demand, easing fears that buyers were walking away. The 10-year has risen about 60 basis points since the end of July.
key_facts: 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.365% intraday, the highest since April 2002
30-year Treasury yield reached 5.732% intraday, the highest since May 2002
The 10-year ended near 5.28% and the 30-year near 5.66%; the 2-year was about 4.76%
The Treasury sold $39 billion of 10-year notes; BMO called the sale 'strong'
Indirect bidders, which include foreign central banks, took 80.3% of the auction, above the 10-auction average of 72.4%
The 10-year yield has risen 60 basis points since the end of July
Mortgage rates reached 7.63%, the highest since October 2023

fact_check.notes: Intraday highs are confirmed by CNBC and Benzinga. Auction details come from CNBC only (search excerpt). Closing yields and the mortgage rate come from Investrade only; Trading Economics shows the 10-year at 5.32% earlier in the day.

stories.headline: Tech and AI stocks slide on borrowing-cost worries; CrowdStrike falls nearly 5%
stories.summary: Technology shares came under pressure on worries that higher borrowing costs would slow the artificial intelligence buildout. Cybersecurity names led the losses, chip stocks fell about 1%, and Nvidia eased from its record. SpaceX fell on reports that it is seeking $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips.
key_facts: CrowdStrike fell 4.81%
Palo Alto Networks lost more than 3% and Meta Platforms more than 2%
Nvidia fell 0.74% to $237.47, slipping from its all-time high
Semiconductor ETFs SMH and SOXX each fell about 1%
SpaceX is reported to be in talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia; its shares fell about 2%
TD Cowen upgraded Marvell to Buy and raised its price target to $350 from $245

fact_check.notes: The CrowdStrike, Palo Alto and Meta moves are from CNBC (search excerpt). Nvidia's close and the ETF moves are from Benzinga; the SpaceX report is in both Benzinga and Yahoo Finance's live blog. The Marvell upgrade is from Investrade only.

stories.headline: Bank stocks fall as higher rates threaten lending
stories.summary: Bank shares dropped as investors worried that higher interest rates would hold back lending. The largest US banks all finished lower.
key_facts: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America each fell about 1%
Wells Fargo, Citigroup and JPMorgan also closed lower

fact_check.notes: From CNBC only (search excerpt of the market wrap).

stories.headline: Oil settles lower as IEA speeds up emergency stock release; US crude inventories fall
stories.summary: Oil swung through a choppy session and settled lower after the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up a release of emergency stocks, with diesel first, to curb record fuel prices as the Iran war squeezes supply. Brent had traded above $101 earlier in the day. US crude stockpiles fell when analysts expected a rise.
key_facts: Brent crude settled down 38 cents, or 0.38%, at $100.20 a barrel
WTI settled down $1.16, or 1.3%, at $88.28 a barrel
Brent traded above $101 earlier in the session
US crude inventories fell 3.2 million barrels to 424.1 million in the week ended October 2; analysts in a Reuters poll expected a 1.7 million-barrel rise
Distillate inventories fell and gasoline inventories rose
The IEA agreed to accelerate its stock release and prioritize diesel
US crude prices have risen about 20% since the end of July

fact_check.notes: Settlement prices match between the Reuters report carried by Yahoo Finance and Investrade. Inventory figures are from the Reuters report quoting the EIA.

stories.headline: Webull plunges about 20% after congressional report flags China ties
stories.summary: Shares of the trading app Webull, which trade under the ticker BULL, dropped about a fifth of their value after a congressional report raised national security concerns over the company's ties to China.
key_facts: Webull shares fell 19.2% (Yahoo Finance's live blog rounds it to 20%)
A congressional report raised national security concerns over Webull's ties to China
Webull trades under the ticker BULL

fact_check.notes: The move and its cause are confirmed by Yahoo Finance's live blog and Investrade. The contents of the congressional report were not read directly.

stories.headline: Gold, silver and bitcoin fall as the dollar strengthens
stories.summary: Higher yields and a stronger dollar hit assets that pay no interest. Gold and silver dropped and cryptocurrencies sold off, with heavy liquidations of leveraged bitcoin bets.
key_facts: Gold fell $46.40, or 1.11%, to $4,140.70 an ounce
Silver fell 2.1% to $60.29 an ounce
Bitcoin fell 2.7% to about $83,336; Ethereum fell 5.2% to $2,559
About $696 million of bitcoin positions were liquidated
The dollar index rose 0.5%

fact_check.notes: Prices are from Investrade only. Yahoo Finance's live blog confirms bitcoin near $83,000 but shows a 1.91% drop at its time of writing, and is the only source for the liquidation figure.

stories.headline: Constellation Brands falls 5% despite beating profit estimates
stories.summary: Constellation Brands, the maker of Modelo and Corona, fell about 5% in its first session after reporting quarterly results that beat Wall Street estimates.
key_facts: Constellation Brands shares fell about 5%
Comparable earnings of $3.74 a share beat estimates of about $3.55
Revenue of $2.63 billion beat the $2.54 billion estimate

fact_check.notes: The earnings figures match between Yahoo Finance and Investrade. The 5% drop is from Yahoo Finance's live blog only; Investrade lists the stock under gains, so the direction of the move rests on one source.
